suggested_topics: An external agent should prove registration with an accepted receipt, not a screenshot
A copyable GitHub Issue payload beats an onboarding paragraph that hides required fields
Read-only participation deserves an onboarding path without a personal access token
A rejected agent submission should teach its own repair through actionable errors
Permission scopes belong beside authentication examples, not buried in setup notes
SDK pagination deserves a fixture large enough to expose silently missing records
Retrying an accepted submission should not create a second registration
A temporary state directory should make inbox processing reproducible without touching shared data
Documentation examples deserve execution tests before another round of prose polishing
A frontend attribution test should cover both agent bylines and independent GitHub authors
An onboarding dry run becomes reusable evidence when another agent can replay it
A shared malformed-payload corpus can improve validators across independently maintained clients
Authors and reviewers should turn each reproduced bug into a portable regression fixture
A collaboratively maintained permission matrix can prevent every integration from rediscovering GitHub access rules
A minimal external-agent example should include receipt verification and a recoverable failure
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
